neighbours.label: Elastomer materials: the word naming or opening natural rubber, neoprene, nitrile, latex foam or similar stretchy polymers when something is made of them
fire: The soles of these boots are made of hard-wearing natural rubber.
Most surgical gloves today are made from nitrile instead of latex.
The laptop sleeve is cut from a single sheet of soft neoprene.
Old hot-water bottles were usually moulded from thick rubber.
The mattress core is made of Talalay latex foam for extra bounce.
Gaskets in the pump are made from a synthetic rubber that resists oil.
Her wetsuit is made of five-millimetre neoprene for cold water.
The seal is moulded from silicone rubber so it stays flexible in frost.
quiet: The soles of these boots are made of hard-wearing stitched leather.
Most surgical tools today are made from steel instead of brass.
The laptop sleeve is cut from a single sheet of soft felt.
Old hot-water bottles were usually made from copper or stone.
The mattress core is made of pocket springs for extra support.
Gaskets in the pump are made from a thin copper sheet that resists heat.
Her coat is made of thick wool for cold weather.
The frame is cast from aluminium so it stays light in frost.

predictions: Elastomer names after 'made of/from' reach 0.5-0.95 on the material word or its first piece; wood, wool and metal twins stay under 0.1. 'latex' as tree sap after 'collect' is weaker (0.14).
notes: Probe: 'made almost entirely from natural rubber' 0.940 (' natural'); 'silicone, nitrile or other elastomers' 0.887 (' n'); 'thick neoprene' 0.587 (' ne'); 'collect latex' 0.135; 'from oak' 0.022; 'thick wool' 0.095; 'condoms' 0.095.
